title: CORRECTION to 20260921T211003508Z-37b573: the ants never build a trail, in any seed
question: With the peak thrown out, is 'the colony cannot hold a route-length trail at all' the right problem to work on next -- or is a blob at the nest plus episodic streaks actually enough, and the thing to fix is elsewhere?
context_md:
**Supersedes the meta on the previous card, which was wrong.** You rejected it on sight: *"ant-laid peak doesn't seem like a good metric... for seed 4 it is caused by a single bright spot not a good trail from nest to food."* Correct -- `max()` over cells cannot see a hole.

Same image. The metric is now the **longest unbroken dark run** along the route, against the ant's own `sensor_offset` of 6, because a gap the animal can see across is not a break.

| seed | cells lit | worst dark gap | route connected |
|---|---|---|---|
| hand-laid, every seed | **91/91** | **0** | **100%** of frames |
| 1 | 0/91 | 91 | 8% |
| 2 | 26/91 | 47 | 8% |
| 3 | 25/91 | 44 | 8% |
| 4 (the "78% peak") | 30/91 | **43** | 8% |

Seed 4 has a **43-cell hole in a 91-cell route**. On peak it looked 4x better than seed 1; on connectivity all four are identical. It is not a distribution -- **no colony builds a nest-to-food trail in any seed.**
